summary: Trinity County summit lookout built to a 1934 Region 5 Plan 4AR design, with a WWII aircraft-warning cabin, fire-season staffing in the 1950s-60s, and good condition in 2009.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan 4AR wooden lookout house on a concrete and rock foundation; an Aircraft Warning Service residence cabin was added in WWII
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Shasta-Trinity National Forest

access.note: Summit road about ten miles in from Highway 3; 4WD needed in the wet season and on the last half mile (2009 report). A road guide says 4WD is required and the road closes October 30 to May 1.

visit.trail_note: About ten miles in from Highway 3; 2WD for most of the road per the 2009 visit report; a road guide says 4WD is required

events.note: Newspaper refers to a Bonanza King lookout station; telephone lines built to it
Lookout injured in a fall while searching for a fire on July 24; died in early August
Register date for the current California Region 5 Plan 4AR lookout house
Lookout Harry Churchman spotted a smoke plume 78 miles from his station and placed it on the Bogard District of the Lassen forest
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the lookout house: wooden, 16 ft square, about 20 ft tall, on a concrete and rock foundation
June Osborne opened the lookout May 20; Jeannie Dickson filling the post by mid-June
Betty Carlson said she had been a lookout every fire season since 1962 (1987 article)
Visit report: lookout in good shape, fresh deck paint, support buildings need paint, encroaching electronic sites
Registered January 3, 2015 as US 1056, CA 101; nominated by Mark Basque

notes_for_editor: Built 1934 from the register; a 1924 newspaper item already refers to a Bonanza King lookout station, so an earlier structure may have existed; not resolved. Access conflict: the 2009 register visit says 2WD for most of the road, while the Dangerous Roads guide says 4WD required and a closure October 30 to May 1 (undated third-party guide). Elevation 6,956 ft (register) vs 6,955 ft (1987 article and guide). The record's kind 'ground' fits the cab-on-foundation description. A Trinity Journal column reporting an AlertCalifornia wildfire camera at the lookout turned up in search but could not be fetched (HTTP 429); not used, worth a recheck for current status. The 1929 lookout injury and death is kept unnamed in the story. Current staffing status after 2009 not confirmed.
